title: The night the sky fell (1833) 🌠
description:
On 13 November 1833 up to ~100,000 shooting stars an hour fell over America, and many thought the world was ending. Yale's Denison Olmsted collected reports through newspapers, saw every streak came from one point in Leo that moved with the stars, and showed meteors come from space. They're dust from comet Tempel-Tuttle; the Leonids peak again on 17-18 November 2026 (~15 an hour).

Sources: Smithsonian Magazine; Linda Hall Library; The Irish Times; Space.com.

meta.topic: the 1833 Leonid meteor storm: up to ~100,000 an hour, panic, Denison Olmsted crowdsourced reports via newspapers, radiant in Leo moving with the stars = from space (birth of meteor science), comet Tempel-Tuttle, ~33-year cycle, 2026 peak ~15/h
meta.idea_source: trending + unique: Leonids peak 17-18 Nov 2026 (Space.com) and the 1833 storm anniversary week; backlog idea (1833 Leonid storm); few Shorts tell the Olmsted crowdsourcing story

humour.trend: timeless dry aside (no current meme fit: 'Remember November' already used twice this week): side-eye + 'the 1833 group chat: u guys seeing this??' card

claims.claim: the 1833 Leonid storm (night of 12-13 Nov) reached ~50,000-150,000 meteors an hour (~100,000)
many who saw it thought it was Judgment Day / the end of the world
meteors radiated from a point in Leo that moved with the stars -> cosmic, not atmospheric; birth of meteor-shower science
the Leonids come from comet Tempel-Tuttle; big displays roughly every 33 years
the sky 'can fall again' on a future return (storms are forecast, not guaranteed)
